The same hazard ratio evidence read against three analysis objectives; what changes is where the confidence interval must fall. The dark dashed line marks *HR = 1* (no difference) and the grey dashed lines the pre-specified margin $\Delta$.[^analysis-objectives]
:::

[^analysis-objectives]: **Analysis objectives on a forest plot.** Each blue square is the point estimate of the hazard ratio (HR) and the horizontal bar its 95% confidence interval (CI). **Superiority** requires the whole CI to lie on the favourable side and to *exclude* HR = 1. **Non-inferiority** requires only that the CI's upper bound stays on the favourable side of the margin - it may cross HR = 1. **Equivalence** requires the entire CI to fall within the symmetric margins $(-\Delta, +\Delta)$ around HR = 1. The direction of benefit depends on the endpoint: here a lower HR (fewer events) favours the new treatment.
